referents.why: 'he said' answers Moses's question 'when shall I pray'; a reply is spoken by the other party, Pharaoh.
referents.category: reply spoken by the other party

referents.why: 'according to your word' refers to Pharaoh's word 'tomorrow', so the second masculine singular is Pharaoh.
'our God' is first plural in Moses's speech. The people of Israel is not a candidate; Moses and Aaron is the nearest first-plural group of speakers. None is also defensible.
'he replied' after Pharaoh's answer: the other party, Moses.
referents.category: reply spoken by the other party

referents.why: second masculine singular 'you may know' in Moses's speech: the addressee, Pharaoh.

links.why: 'that there is no one like the LORD' is what is to be known, the object of yada.
links.category: that-clause after a verb of knowing

links.why: lemaan plus yiqtol in a different person gives the purpose of the wish 'may it be according to your word'. The wish is nominal, not an imperative, so the fit is not exact.
cl0 is the first clause of the verse and cl4 is the last clause of Moses's speech. An and-then runs forward from the earlier clause, so this link runs backward.
cl1 sits inside Pharaoh's speech. A wayyiqtol continues the narrative line from the nearest clause before it that is not inside a speech, here cl0.
links.category: narrative then from inside a speech

links.why: 'he replied' continues the frame of Pharaoh's speech (cl0), the nearest clause before it outside any speech.
'he said' introduces Pharaoh's answer 'tomorrow'; cl1 is the said clause.
'he replied' introduces Moses's words, which begin with 'according to your word'.

groups.why: The builder gave the sender as cl0s, a slot and not a person. The speaker is Pharaoh; the addressee was missing and is Moses, whose question he answers.
The builder gave the sender as cl2s, a slot and not a person. The speaker is Moses, addressing Pharaoh; the addressee was missing.
